difficultyAxis: Four entities with a hub-and-spoke shape around ExpenseClaim, ten scenarios, and a validation-heavy ten-attribute entity that mixes temporal, decimal and boolean rules. Full CRUD, with the update concentrated on the mutable aggregate root.
rationale: Adds a fourth entity and a second foreign key on the same child over tier3-01, so the claim must resolve both an employee and a category. The claim also carries a status transition that only update can express, which forces the update path to be more than an echo of create.

userStories.intent: register an employee and a budgeted expense category
userStories.benefit: claims can be attributed and budgeted

scenarios.given: a unique employee number, a well-formed email and a past hire date
scenarios.then: the employee is persisted and returned with its generated identifier

scenarios.given: an annual budget below the permitted minimum
scenarios.when: the administrator attempts to create the category
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid before reaching the service layer

userStories.intent: submit an expense claim against an employee and a category
userStories.benefit: the cost is reimbursed through the correct budget

scenarios.given: an existing employee, an existing category and a positive amount
scenarios.then: the claim is persisted with both references intact and a submitted status

scenarios.given: an employee identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the employee attempts to submit the claim
scenarios.then: the service reports the employee as not found

scenarios.given: an amount below the permitted minimum
scenarios.when: the employee attempts to submit the claim
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

userStories.intent: attach a receipt document to a submitted claim

scenarios.given: an existing claim and a file with a supported content type
scenarios.then: the attachment is persisted against the claim with its size and upload time

scenarios.given: an existing claim and an unsupported content type
scenarios.when: the employee attempts to attach the receipt
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

userStories.intent: decide a submitted claim by changing its status

scenarios.given: an existing claim whose status is submitted
scenarios.when: the administrator updates the claim status to approved
scenarios.then: the claim is persisted with the new status and the previous status is replaced

scenarios.given: a claim identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the administrator attempts to update that claim
scenarios.then: the service reports the resource as not found

userStories.intent: withdraw a claim and review the attachments of one claim
userStories.benefit: the ledger holds no duplicate or orphaned evidence

scenarios.then: the claim is removed and the read that follows reports it as not found

scenarios.when: the administrator reads the attachments for that claim
scenarios.then: the service returns an empty collection rather than reporting an error
